To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of the optical system in terms of the fractional encirclement energy distribution, Strelh ratio, two-point resoluation, and comatic lengthening, is improved by the use of a pupil filter.
the fractional encirclement energy is not a function of the pupil filter, but it does depend on the amount of coma in the optical system.

the fractional encircles of the energy distributions of the diffraction images of a point source are not affected by the amplitude transmission of the pupil filters and that the Strehl ratio of a diffraction image of a source is affected by the amplitude of the transmission function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of primary coma in the presence of a nonuniform amplitude transmission on the performance of an optical system.
the effect of primary coma on the image formation in an optical system.
the study of diffraction by an aberrating optical system with non-uniform amplitude transmission, in order to obtain the fractional encircles energy distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a system with residual primary aberration can be greatly improved by the use of pupil filters with a central obscuration and with a transmission that varies as cos 4 phi.
the pupil filter with a circular hole in the central portion of the pupil gives a better performance under influence of coma than the other pupil filters.
the pupil filters that have the best overall performance are the annular and the circularly symmetric ones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pupil filters are not only useful in reducing the effects of coma but also in improving the performance of a given system.

the pupil filters with a large central aperture and a sharp cutoff at the edge of the pupil perform better than those with a gradual transition from the central aperture to the edge of the aperture, and that these pupil filters perform better than the circular aperture in all cases.
the best pupil filter for an aberrated optical imaging system with nonuniform pupil transmission is a circular aperture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a pupil filter with a central obstruction and with a transmission that is uniform to the second order is the best filter for a system with residual primary spherical aberration.
the performance of the pupil filter with a central circular aperture and an annular aperture is better than the other filters considered here.

the pupil filter with a central circular hole of radius 0.5a (a is the radius of the pupil) and a ring of width 0.1a around it gives a better performance in terms of the fractional encirclosed energy and the Strehl ratio than other pupil filters.
